absent: Locking, concurrency and interrupt safety for slot tables, stash publication, transient allocator and image restore are not shown.
Numeric values and bit layouts for suspend offsets, hash fields, page flag transforms, vector length, debug control encoding and length masks are not shown.
Internals of low level suspend, identity map handling, CNP, PAN, DIT, speculation mitigation, SME, pointer authentication, EL2 reset detection and safe page allocation are not shown.
Unit discovery, debug monitor enable accounting and perf integration beyond install hooks are not shown.
Cold versus warm boot detection and error handling beyond allocation and validation failures are not shown.

findings.text: Suspend entry preserves the caller frame and callee saved registers into a caller supplied buffer, records the current stack pointer in the system area, hashes the processor affinity identifier with global mask and shift tables to index a global stash and publish the buffer there, then calls the low level suspend helper on the system area and reports direct return with success.
Stash publication uses eight byte slots indexed by the hashed affinity value and happens before the low level suspend call, allowing resume to find the saved context by CPU identity.

Resume exit restores processor state in a fixed sequence: tagging setup, identity map removal, common translation bit restore when supported, DIT and access prevention handling, breakpoint register restore through a hook when registered, speculation mitigation enforcement, then matrix and authentication restoration.
Tagging resume work is entirely skipped when the platform does not advertise support, otherwise per CPU tagging setup runs.
A predicate reports CPUs retained in the kernel when a stuck flag is set, when more than one CPU is possible without a die operation, or when protected virtualization is active.
Die capability exists only in hotplug builds when the current CPU operation vector is present and supplies a die callback.

Hibernation resume creates a temporary duplicate of the linear mapping with atomic allocation, obtains a zero page that must stay zero across restore, optionally duplicates hypervisor vectors when a reset is needed, relocates the exit trampoline to a safe executable page, installs temporary vectors when needed, then jumps to the trampoline with physical addresses and saved state and never returns.

The relocated exit code cannot take exceptions and the suspended image expects masked asynchronous interrupts, so all such interrupts are masked immediately before transfer and the fall through is unreachable; table, zero page, vector or safe page allocation failures abort with an error.
A minimal hypervisor stub forwards its address argument using the set vectors hypercall identifier.
Transient table creation allocates an empty top table then duplicates a kernel virtual range into it, propagating allocation failure and publishing the destination only on success.
Top level duplication walks the source kernel range in successive chunks, skips empty entries and delegates populated entries to the next level until the end address is reached.

Four nested helpers implement one translation level each: each ensures a destination intermediate table exists by allocating on demand, then iterates its subrange and either recurses for table entries or installs a converted leaf; the leaf level always allocates a fresh destination page before copying.
Copied block and page leaves are installed as valid kernel writable mappings without virtual area accounting, while empty source entries leave the destination untouched.

Vector duplication allocates one transient page, returns its physical address, copies the full stub vector length from the dedicated area, then cleans that range to unification and to coherency points.
Non boot CPU handling for resume fails when the suspend CPU is unknown and otherwise freezes secondary CPUs targeting that CPU.

Each CPU keeps separate pointer tables for installed instruction breakpoints and data watchpoints plus a flag for kernel breakpoint stepping, with global counters for breakpoint and watchpoint unit counts.

A slot query returns the breakpoint count for instruction type and the watchpoint count for data type by probing hardware directly so early callers avoid uninitialized globals, warning and returning zero for unknown types.
Compatibility classification treats events without a target task as native and otherwise follows the target thread state, avoiding deprecated unaligned behavior for per CPU events.
Slot management supports occupy first empty, clear matching, and locate matching without mutation; unknown operations warn once and fail, and exhaustion or no match fails.

Breakpoint control selects instruction or data register banks, slot tables, capacity limits and enable state from per thread disable flags plus privilege derived level, then on install enables monitors and programs address and encoded control, on restore reprograms both, and on uninstall clears control and releases monitors, warning when no slot is found.
Architecture install and uninstall are thin wrappers forwarding to control with install and uninstall operations.
Length decoding maps eight distinct encodings to one through eight bytes, and kernel space testing treats a range as kernel when both its start and inclusive end reach the user limit.
A breakpoint description carries an address plus control state with access kind, length mask, privilege level and enable flag.
Generic translation validates access kind and nonzero length, derives an offset from the lowest set length bit, then maps normalized length to generic length codes, rejecting unknown combinations.

Construction from generic attributes maps access kind to execute and load store combinations and length to matching encodings, restricts native execute to four bytes with fixup and compatible execute to two or four bytes, records the requested address, assigns privilege by the kernel space test, and enables according to the disabled attribute.

Parsing enforces alignment after construction: compatible events use a small mask selected by length and accept only defined offset pairings for halfword and byte cases, native execute uses a smaller mask than native data, overflow of shifted length beyond the control field is rejected, then the address is aligned down and length shifted by the offset, and privileged events bound to a task are rejected.
Truncation of shifted length would program fewer bytes than requested, so overflow is invalid, and per task kernel breakpoints are refused because they would complicate stepping.
Thread switch compares disable flags between outgoing and incoming threads and toggles breakpoint and watchpoint banks at user level only when the corresponding flag differs.

Reset walks all breakpoint and watchpoint slots on the current CPU, restoring occupied entries and zeroing control and value for empty ones, serving cold boot with no entries, hotplug with empty tables, and warm boot with retained entries.
Slot operation identifiers comprise install, uninstall and restore states.
Debug register access dispatches on base plus index to per index read and write helpers.
Diagnostic output for this subsystem uses a fixed identifying textual prefix.
